title: No-profile S3 startup error is immediately overwritten

evidence.quote: showInlineMessage("Choose a profile and region to list buckets, or enter a bucket manually.")

reasoning: When no AWS profiles are configured, reloadProfiles correctly shows the noProfiles error, but viewDidLoad always calls renderIdleState immediately afterward. renderIdleState clears lastError, hides retry/details, and replaces the actionable error with a generic idle prompt, so a first-run user loses the real setup failure.
reproduction: Launch the S3 browser on a machine/user account with no AWS profiles. The controller calls showInlineError(.noProfiles) and then immediately replaces it with the idle message.
recommendation: Only render the idle state when profiles were loaded, or have reloadProfiles return a state/result so viewDidLoad does not overwrite terminal setup errors.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included BrowserCapabilityTests cover S3 menus and region helpers, and S3BrowserServiceTests cover service/transfer behavior; there is no controller startup test for an empty AWSProfileStore.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a controller-level test with an injected empty AWSProfileStore that calls viewDidLoad/loadViewIfNeeded and asserts the status label or error state still reports no profiles after startup.

history.reasoning: The original evidence path still exists, but the startup flow has changed. In Grove/Controllers/S3BrowserViewController.swift, viewDidLoad now calls renderIdleState() only inside if reloadProfiles() returns true. reloadProfiles() now returns false immediately after showInlineError(.noProfiles) when profiles.isEmpty, so the no-profile error is no longer immediately overwritten by the idle message. showInlineError also preserves lastError and sets the status/empty labels to the error text. I found no controller-level regression test for this exact startup state; the relevant existing tests cover profile parsing, S3 service behavior, and capability helpers. Attempting xcodebuild test was blocked by the read-only sandbox because Xcode could not create cache/log/SourcePackages files under /tmp, so the classification is based on current code flow plus test coverage inspection.
